About Tucson Pool Cleaning Pro

One free number and a set of plain guides for pool owners from Oro Valley down to Green Valley. The line puts you in touch with an independent local pool company. It never does pool work itself.

Call (520) 372-1083 See how a call works

A phone line, not a pool company

Tucson Pool Cleaning Pro is a d/b/a of Dominion Digital Group. It is a free phone number plus this website, and that is the whole operation.

There is no shop, no fleet and no crew behind the name. Nobody from the line will come to your house, test your water, look at your pump or hand you a price. What the line does is answer the phone at any hour, find out in a sentence or two what the pool is doing, and hand the call to a separate, locally owned pool business serving the Tucson area.

That company is the one that visits, figures out what is wrong, quotes the job and does it. It bills you itself. The line has no seat at that table and does not step in to set prices, dates or terms.

Spelling this out may seem like a lot of fuss over a phone number. It matters because plenty of pool websites read as if they belong to a company with trucks on the road. This one does not, and you should know who you are dealing with before you dial.

Why one number for every kind of pool problem

Pool trouble in the Tucson area comes in a lot of shapes, and it often shows up at a bad time. The line exists so you do not have to work out who to call first.

Problems do not keep office hours

A pump that quits on a 105 degree Saturday or a yard full of debris after a late monsoon storm cannot wait for Monday. The assistant picks up at every hour, on every day of the week, and if the company cannot take the call right then, it receives your details and can return the call.

One call covers most pool needs

Weekly cleaning, a green pool, calcium on the tile, a leak, a dead light, a noisy pump: you do not need to sort the job into a category first. Describe what you see and the call goes on from there.

A local company hears it first

The transfer goes to an independent, locally owned Tucson-area pool company, not a national call center. It gets a short summary of your problem before it picks up, so you are not starting from zero.

Help checking who you hire

Arizona's Registrar of Contractors keeps a public record of contractor licenses and complaints. This site walks you through searching that record, so the decision to hire stays yours and rests on facts you checked.

What happens when you dial

The process is short on purpose. Here is the whole path from your first ring to a pool company on the line:

  1. Dial the line(520) 372-1083 is picked up by an automated assistant around the clock, holidays included.
  2. Say what the pool is doingGreen water, a pump that is silent or grinding, a light that will not come on, white crust on the tile, plus the part of the Tucson area you live in.
  3. Get transferredYour call is handed to a pool service company in the Tucson area that is independent and locally owned. It gets a quick summary of the problem before it says hello.
  4. Work it out with themThat company inspects, quotes, does the job and bills you itself. If nobody picks up, your name, number, area and pool problem go to the company so it can phone you back.

It helps to know a few things before you call: roughly when the problem started, what you have noticed (water color, sounds from the equipment, a water level that keeps dropping), and which part of the metro the pool is in, such as Rita Ranch, Oro Valley, Vail or the Catalina Foothills. The how it works page covers the call step by step, and the contact page lists what to have handy.

How the line is paid, in plain terms

Calling costs you nothing, and the line never sends you a bill. Pool businesses receiving the calls can pay the line something for each referral. That arrangement is the reason the number can be free, and it is disclosed at the bottom of every page on this site.

The referral fee is between the line and the company. Your price is between you and the company. Ask for the quote in writing, ask what it includes, and compare it with the published ranges in the Tucson pool service cost guide if you want a sense of the market. If a price does not sit right with you, you can turn it down and keep looking.

What you will not see on this site, and why

You will not find star ratings, customer counts, a founding date, staff photos or a list of credentials here. The line does not do pool jobs, so it has nothing truthful to put in those spots, and it will not make them up. For the same reason, it never describes any pool business as licensed, insured, certified or highly rated. It has not checked, so it stays quiet on all of that.

What the site offers instead is a way to check for yourself. Arizona's Registrar of Contractors (ROC) keeps contractor licenses in a public database that anyone can search. The ROC does not require contractors to carry liability insurance, workers' compensation aside, so ask the company directly for proof of coverage if that matters to you.

Get a company's ROC number before repair or equipment work and type it into the ROC license lookup. The record shows whether the license is active, its classification, such as R-6 for residential pool service and repair, and recent complaints. Checking is up to you, because the line does not do it.

Guides written for pools in the Sonoran Desert

The other half of this site is reading material. Pools here deal with conditions that generic pool advice skips: long stretches of triple-digit heat, a monsoon season that the National Weather Service in Tucson dates from June 15 to September 30, and tap water that Tucson Water says gets harder as the share of Central Arizona Project (CAP) supply, which starts as Colorado River water, goes up in the blend. Each guide lists the sources it relies on so you can check them.

Common questions

Does Tucson Pool Cleaning Pro do the pool work itself?

No. It is a phone line and a website. There are no service vehicles, no pool chemicals and no crew behind it, and nobody from the line does pool work of any kind. Your call is handed to a separate pool business based in the Tucson area, and that business handles the visit and the job.

Who owns Tucson Pool Cleaning Pro?

Dominion Digital Group. Tucson Pool Cleaning Pro is a d/b/a (doing business as) name of that company. The pool companies callers are put through to are separate, independent businesses.

If the call is free, how does the line make money?

The pool businesses that take these calls can pay the line a fee for each referral. Callers never owe the line a cent. Whatever price you are quoted is set by the company quoting it, and that company is the one you pay.

Does the line check whether a pool company is licensed?

No, and it does not vouch for any company's license, insurance or credentials. Before repair or equipment work, get the company's license number and enter it in the Registrar of Contractors' online license lookup yourself.

Why does the site have no reviews, team photos or years in business?

Because none of those would be honest. The line does not do pool jobs, so it has no customers' pools to show and no crew to introduce. Judge a pool company by what it tells you, its written quote, its ROC record and the reviews it has earned on independent sites.

Have a pool problem right now?

It is one free call, day or night. Tell the assistant what the pool is doing and which part of the Tucson area it is in, and you are transferred to a local, independently owned pool company that looks at the pool in person and names its own price.
